current_f2_contracts_reused: browser/structural/<target_id> remains the logical source identity
captured_monotonic_ns and temporal-fusion uncertainty remain timing authority
browser observations remain candidate perception rather than canonical truth/effect authority

mapped_policy.name: BROWSER_STRUCTURAL_SELECTIVE_CAPTURE/v1
mapped_policy.default_rationale: AX directly exposes role/name/description/value/widget-state plus DOM/frame linkage and supports depth-bounded, partial and query retrieval; this matches many interaction-oriented structural needs without requiring the full layout/style surface.
domsnapshot_escalation_conditions: requested evidence requires exact DOM attributes or markup structure not represented by AX
requested evidence requires layout bounds, paint order, rectangles or computed-style information
AX result is absent/ignored/ambiguous for a node that remains relevant in rendered perception
cross-check is required between semantic accessibility state and underlying DOM/layout state
a deterministic downstream contract explicitly declares DOM_SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED
ax_modes: getFullAXTree with explicit bounded depth when full semantic hierarchy is justified
avoid persistent Accessibility.enable by default until exact-browser measurement justifies its stable-ID benefit versus the protocol's stated performance impact

anti_authority_rules: AX role/name/state is browser-derived observation, not world fact.
DOMSnapshot clickability/layout is browser-derived observation, not effect authority.
A model may request an escalation candidate but may not silently redefine capture policy or mint canonical state.
AX and DOMSnapshot outputs from the same target/session are not automatically simultaneous; temporal fusion still governs correlation.

efficiency_assessment.source_level: AX has a semantically narrower schema and offers bounded/partial/query retrieval, while DOMSnapshot returns full DOM plus layout and selected style data.
efficiency_assessment.reason: No exact target-browser payload-size, latency, CPU/RSS or steady-state measurement exists in this Trigger-6 macrocycle.
required_measurements: serialized bytes and node counts by representative page
browser CPU/RSS impact with stateless AX calls and with Accessibility.enable
semantic task coverage and fallback rate from AX to DOMSnapshot

expected_benefit: Potentially keep the structural path interaction-focused and small while retaining deterministic escalation to full DOM/layout evidence only when required.
counterhypotheses: Fallback frequency may be high enough that AX-first increases total calls and latency.
Accessibility.enable or repeated AX computation may cost more than one DOMSnapshot at the required cadence.
AX semantics may miss visually actionable but accessibility-ignored nodes, making rendered+DOMSnapshot a more reliable base pair.
A direct DOM query projection could be thinner than either full AX or full DOMSnapshot.
next_discriminator: E3/E4 only on an exact target-browser fixture: collect paired AX and DOMSnapshot observations over representative static, dynamic, form-heavy, canvas-heavy and accessibility-poor pages; measure bytes/latency/CPU/RSS and task coverage while preserving navigation generation fences. Do not call the selective policy efficient until those measurements support it.
